2.39 : 1Scope

Drag across the frame, or use the arrow keys

Scope

The cinematic default for big stories. It gives up height for width, so it suits landscapes, cities and people sharing a shot from far apart.

In the movies
Blade Runner 2049 (2017)
Fun fact
Scope is shot with anamorphic lenses, which squeeze the image sideways and stretch it back later. That is why you see oval blurred highlights and long horizontal flares.

Notes

Watching movies is one of my favorite hobbies, and it changed how I design. I notice the frame before the plot: where the edges sit, what gets cropped, and how much room a shot leaves to breathe. A screen layout makes the same decisions.

Narrow the frame to 4:3 and the lighthouse on the right drops out of the picture. Nothing in the scene changed, only what it showed.

The bars move on a spring rather than a fixed curve, so every change, even mid-drag, reads as one continuous motion.
